pages.text: "I'm done! I'm going to play!" Mina pushed away the empty plate and stood. The sun was just rising over the river. Low water had exposed the bottom step.
Mom offered a tooth-cleaning twig. "Brush first." "Can't I skip just one day?" Mina shook their head and headed to the steps.
While Mom rinsed a towel on the lower step, Mina played. All through the game, something tickled between their teeth. Breakfast bread was stuck there.
Experienced eldest child Raju smiled from above, teeth sparkling white. "Why are yours so white?" Mina asked.
"I clean them every morning." Raju waved the twig. "If you don't, crumbs stay between your teeth." Mina felt with their tongue. Something really was caught.
They sat together on the lowest step, Mom standing beside them. "Up, then down. Copy me." Raju brushed first. Mina put the twig in their mouth, too.
Brush, brush! Front teeth, back molars! The tickling crumbs washed away in the river water. Mina brushed happily. "Brush, Brush, Teeth Shining White!"
Mina opened wide, showing clean teeth. Mom looked inside. "Crumbs left there all night can make your teeth hurt."
The next morning, Mina got the cleaning twig first. "Raju, I'll brush with you!"
Raju put an arm around Mina's shoulders as they climbed the steps. Mina smiled, teeth showing. "No bread is stuck now!"
